inspection_summary: Inspected all 786 normalized lines. The source develops a coherent Poisson/exponential-generating-function bridge between the Riesz function R(x) and the Baez-Duarte sequence c_k, proves the two growth criteria equivalent through a forward transform and a quantified integer-sampling approximation, relates c_k oscillations to zeta zeros, and records useful but partly heuristic consequences for alternating and ordinary partial sums and for self-consistency of R. Formula prose is recoverable, while the extracted plots retain captions and axes but not enough visual content for curve-level evidence.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the bidirectional R(x)-to-c_k program and the alternating-sum application.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the two RH criteria and formulates their parameterized growth-rate duality.

sections_inspected.label: 2. Some facts on R(x) and c_k
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Gives accelerated Mobius representations, computational motivation, and a zero-driven asymptotic picture for c_k.

sections_inspected.label: Forward-difference and exponential-transform construction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Identifies c_k as finite differences and derives the exact exponential generating transform reconstructing R(x).

sections_inspected.label: Theorem 1 and equivalence proof
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Transfers decay from c_k to growth of R and conversely via a quantified approximation at integer arguments.

sections_inspected.label: Approximation interpretation and numerical comparison
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Explains c_k approximately equal to R(k)/k by matching a binomial kernel with an exponential kernel.

sections_inspected.label: 4. Some other relations
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives an alternating-sum identity and a parameterized family, then diagnoses failure of a formal unweighted summation.

sections_inspected.label: Partial-sum conjectures and approximate self-constraints
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses numerical oscillations and the c_k-to-R(k) approximation to propose partial-sum rates and discrete self-relations for R.

sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bounds the binomial-versus-exponential kernel error and proves the O(k^{-3/2}) control needed for the reverse implication.

accepted_units.title: Parameterized duality of the Riesz and Baez-Duarte criteria
accepted_units.why_material: Places the continuous Riesz growth criterion and discrete Baez-Duarte decay criterion into the reusable paired form c_k=O(k^{-delta}) iff R(x)=O(x^{1-delta}), making the shift by one exponent explicit rather than relying only on transitivity through RH.
accepted_units.context_note: Carried unchanged from v1; the span contains both definitions, their RH specializations, and the announced generalization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (2)--(5) are needed, but their mathematical content is recoverable from the extracted formulas and prose.

accepted_units.title: Mobius-exponential representation of the Riesz function
accepted_units.why_material: Replaces a slowly convergent zeta-reciprocal power series by a Mobius-weighted exponential sum, a representation change that later makes comparison with the binomial formula for c_k possible.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the first Kummer-accelerated formula; lines 195--207 define the Mobius weights and give the repeated-acceleration variant used by the carried computational unit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula (6) is legible in extraction; interpretation depends on reading its displayed sum together with the surrounding prose.

accepted_units.unit_type: accelerated formulas and first-zero wave picture
accepted_units.title: Accelerated computation and zero-spectrum oscillations of c_k
accepted_units.why_material: Connects accelerated computation of R(x) with an explicit large-k expression for c_k indexed by nontrivial zeta zeros, including exponential suppression of higher ordinates and the resulting first-zero cosine-like behavior in log k.
accepted_units.context_note: Carried unchanged from v1. Its opening repeats Kummer's procedure and therefore needs lines 98--109 and 195--201 as v2 context; the Fig. 3 image itself is not recoverable from text, but the qualitative oscillation claim is stated in prose.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed formulas (8)--(13) are recoverable with minor text-layer layout risk; scan verification would be required for curve-level claims from Fig. 3, not for the stated first-zero mechanism.

accepted_units.title: Poisson transform from finite differences c_k to R(x)
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that c_k is the first entry in iterated forward differences of f(k)=1/zeta(2k+2), then exponentiates the shift operator to obtain the exact identity sum c_k x^k/k!=e^x R(x)/x. This is the structural bridge behind the continuous-discrete duality.
accepted_units.context_note: The span is self-contained from the difference table through the exact reconstruction identity and the stated duality.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The operator and generating-function displays (14)--(18) are essential and recoverable, though superscripts and fraction placement should be checked against the normalized lines when reused.

accepted_units.title: Forward growth transfer from c_k to R(x)
accepted_units.why_material: States the general equivalence theorem and proves the c_k-to-R direction by combining the exact exponential transform with a coefficient-weight asymptotic for sum k^{-delta}x^k/k!, exposing Poisson smoothing as the source of the exponent shift.
accepted_units.context_note: Carried unchanged from v1. The theorem's setup begins at line 331 and its converse is completed at lines 396--413, so the immutable v1 span requires that bounded surrounding context in v2.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The coefficient asymptotic and inequalities (19)--(25) are legible enough for the mechanism; exact reuse should preserve the displayed exponent signs.

accepted_units.title: Recovering c_k decay from integer samples of R
accepted_units.why_material: Completes the converse by combining R(k)=O(k^{1-delta}) with the appendix bound between c_k and R(k)/k; it also makes explicit why the available error restricts the proved transfer to delta<3/2.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the missing converse of the carried theorem unit and relies on the appendix proof at lines 646--737.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula (26) has text-layer fraction-placement risk, but lines 407--412 disambiguate it as |R(k)/k-c_k|=O(k^{-3/2}).

accepted_units.title: Binomial-to-exponential explanation of c_k approximately equal to R(k)/k
accepted_units.why_material: Rewrites c_k as a Mobius-weighted binomial-kernel sum and approximates (1-1/n^2)^k by exp(-k/n^2), directly matching the accelerated Riesz representation at x=k. This supplies an interpretable de-Poissonization heuristic later made quantitative.
accepted_units.context_note: The preceding numerical fit motivates the approximation but is not required for the kernel comparison; the appendix supplies the rigorous error estimate.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formulas (28)--(29) are central and recoverable; the approximation is explicitly heuristic in this span.

accepted_units.unit_type: alternating sums and divergent total sum
accepted_units.title: Weighted generating family and the obstruction to formal unweighted summation
accepted_units.why_material: Derives the alternating sum from the Mobius/binomial representation, embeds it in a parameterized generating identity with asymmetric convergence domains, and contrasts it with a formal shift-operator evaluation of sum c_k whose predicted value is defeated by growing oscillations.
accepted_units.context_note: Carried unchanged from v1. Because the first derivation invokes formula (28), lines 424--444 are needed as bounded context; the span itself contains the convergence warning and the empirical divergence diagnosis.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The generating identities (30)--(35) are recoverable; the late partial-sum evidence is prose-supported, while its plotted realization follows outside the span.

accepted_units.title: Contrasting asymptotics for alternating and ordinary partial sums
accepted_units.why_material: Distinguishes a convergent alternating accumulation, conjectured to approach its limit at c_k-like rate, from an ordinary partial sum conjectured to oscillate with growing n^{1/4} scale. This records a falsifiable consequence rather than treating formal summation as convergence.
accepted_units.context_note: The claims are explicitly speculative and rest on the numerical observations in lines 553--600 plus the first-zero approximation, not on a proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (36)--(37) are legible; the associated plotted curve is not recoverable from the text layer and would need scan verification for quantitative visual evidence.

accepted_units.title: Discrete self-entanglement constraint for the Riesz function
accepted_units.why_material: Substituting c_k approximately equal to R(k)/k into the exact generating transform yields an approximate reconstruction of R(x) from its positive-integer values, turning the continuous-discrete bridge into a potential self-consistency constraint rather than merely a criterion equivalence.
accepted_units.context_note: The span also records the underlying comparison of two zeta-reciprocal sums and labels the final proof relevance as an open question.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula (39) is recoverable but its exact normalization depends on the displayed layout; reuse should verify the e^x/x factor against the source.

accepted_units.title: Uniform kernel-error bound for c_k versus R(k)/k
accepted_units.why_material: Controls the difference between exponential and binomial kernels by removing Mobius signs, bounding a unimodal summand by its maximum plus an integral, and estimating that integral through Gaussian and beta-function asymptotics. The resulting leading O(k^{-3/2}) error is the quantitative de-Poissonization step enabling the reverse criterion implication.
accepted_units.context_note: This appendix supplies the deferred proof of formula (26); lower-order exponential and k^{-5/2} terms are retained before simplifying for k>16.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several displays have fraction and radical layout risk, but the prose and final inequality make the leading k^{-3/2} bound recoverable; exact constants should be scan-checked before formal reuse.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Poissonization and quantified de-Poissonization as the equivalence mechanism
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The exact exponential transform smooths discrete c_k decay into R(x) growth, while the O(k^{-3/2}) integer-sampling error reverses the transfer; the paired mechanisms explain both the one-power exponent shift and the delta<3/2 proof range.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The reverse transfer is tied to the proved approximation rate and to integer samples; it does not by itself improve the RH-relevant exponent or establish RH.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Zero-driven oscillations propagate from coefficients to cumulative behavior
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A first-zero-dominated log-periodic model for c_k qualitatively explains both cosine-like coefficient oscillations and why ordinary accumulation can diverge while alternating accumulation converges.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The zero expansion is presented under assumptions on zeros, and the partial-sum rates are numerical speculation rather than proved asymptotics.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Kernel matching yields a self-consistency view of R
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Matching the binomial kernel for c_k to the exponential kernel for R(k)/k, then feeding that approximation through the exact transform, makes R approximately reconstructible from its integer values and isolates the reconstruction error.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The final self-entanglement relation remains approximate and the paper leaves open whether it is strong enough to prove the Riesz growth bound.
